newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANDELSBANKEN SETS OUT ESTONIA PLANS.
newsitem.headline: HANDELSBANKEN SETS OUT ESTONIA PLANS.

text.p: Sweden's largest bank Handelsbanken said on Monday that it was aiming for a 10 percent share of the Estonian broking and corporate finance market and would like to be a pan-Baltic broker after three years.
Handelsbanken earlier announced that it has bought Estonian broker Aktoris, the first foreign company to enter the Estonian brokerage market.
"I think that 10 percent (market share) and that is a conservative estimate," Auli Kumpulainen, managing director of Aktoris, told a news conference.
Bo Kragh, head of Handelsbanken's representative office said that it was naturally the bank's ambition to have a brokerage operation that would operate in all three Baltic states.
"In two to three years, naturally it is our ambtionn" Kragh said.
The Handelsbanken and Aktoris officials would not reveal how much the Swedish bank had paid for the Estonian broker nor how much Handelsbanken intended to investment.
They also said they could not yet predict the time of their move to Latvia and Lithuania as this depended on economic and political conditions in the two countries.
Handelsbanken's move is the first by a foreign bank into the Baltic brokerage market and comes as Western interest to the Baltics increases.
Many Western banks and institutions have invested into the markets of all three countries, especially Estonia, which is seen as the most liquid of the three countries.

Handelsbanken earlier said that it bought Aktoris as the Estonian firm had been active in the new issues market, having carried out share emissions by construction group EMV and by Tartu Brewery, in which Finnish Olvi has a stake.
